test_title: SSC CGL 2022 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On : 08 Dec 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A mixture contains milk and water in the ratio of 5 ∶ 3, respectively. On adding 7 litres of water, the ratio of milk to water becomes 1 ∶ 2. Find the quantity of milk in the mixture.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Initial Ratio (Milk : Water) = 5 : 3

New Ratio (Milk : Water) = 1 : 2

Multiply New Ratio by 5 to make Milk constant → (1 × 5) : (2 × 5) = 5 : 10

Change in Water units = 10 − 3 = 7 units

Given 7 units = 7 litres ∴ 1 unit = 1 litre

Quantity of Milk = 5 units = 5 × 1 = 5 litres

**∴ The correct answer is 5 litres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial Milk : Water = 5 : 3

Water added = 7 litres

Final Milk : Water = 1 : 2

 Milk (5x) Water (3x) Initial Mixture (5 : 3) 
• + 7 Litres Water Milk (5x) Water (3x + 7) Final Mixture (1 : 2) 

Let the initial quantity of Milk be 5x and Water be 3x.

⇒ New quantity of Water = 3x + 7

⇒ New Ratio = 5x / (3x + 7) = 1 / 2

⇒ 2 × (5x) = 1 × (3x + 7)

⇒ 10x = 3x + 7

⇒ 10x − 3x = 7

⇒ 7x = 7

⇒ x = 1

⇒ Quantity of Milk = 5x = 5 × 1 = 5 litres

**∴ The correct answer is 5 litres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Alligation Rule

A rule used to find the ratio in which two or more ingredients at their respective prices/concentrations are mixed to produce a mixture at a given mean price/concentration.

Component Balance

When one component (like milk) is not added or removed, its absolute quantity remains constant even if the total mixture volume and ratios change.

Ratio Scaling

To compare or combine ratios, multiply terms by a common factor to equalize the parts of a shared component (e.g., matching milk units in two different ratios).
